issues.description: Loop invariant / offset semantics are not stated in code; reader must infer `from <color>` grammar
issues.detail: The fix introduces `offset = isRelativeColor ? 2 : 0`, but the comment only motivates the 2nd-value start without naming the invariant: after `from`, args[1] is the source color and channel args begin at index 2. A literate one-line invariant above the offset line would make this auditable without re-reading the CSS Color 5 spec.

issues.description: Detection of relative color syntax is asymptotically OK but practically fragile: only checks args[0].value === 'from'
issues.detail: `args` is filtered to `word|function`; a stray token type, leading comment node, or unusual whitespace handling upstream by postcss-value-parser could shift indexing. The check assumes the parser always places `from` as args[0]. Worth either asserting this or scanning for a `from` word token explicitly to avoid silent off-by-one when grammar evolves.

issues.description: `args[0 + offset]` and `args[2 + offset]` obscure intent; a named index would read better
issues.detail: Writing `args[0 + offset]` is a tell that the author is documenting the offset inline. A small literate decomposition — `const hueIndex = (HUE_FIRST_ARG_FUNCS.includes(value) ? 0 : 2) + offset;` with one return — makes the indexing arithmetic explicit and removes the `0 + offset` curiosity. Pure readability, no behavior change.

issues.description: No test covers nested relative color where the outer function is hue-first (hsl/hwb) with from + nested function
issues.detail: There is one mixed nested case for the lch-inside-hsl with both warnings, which is good. Missing: a nested relative color where the inner color is itself `from`, e.g. `oklch(from oklch(from red l c h) l c h)`. The offset logic recurses correctly only if walker descends; a single test would prove termination on nested relative chains.

issues.description: `args[0]?.value.toLowerCase()` recomputed even when args is empty; minor but worth a guard comment
issues.detail: Optional chaining handles undefined, but for an empty `args` array the function silently returns `undefined` from both branches because `args[offset]` is undefined. That is correct behavior, but a one-line comment confirming `findHue` returns undefined for malformed input would document the contract for the caller and any future reader.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED but essentially correct. The fix is small, targeted, and the test matrix meaningfully covers the false-negative and false-positive directions including a case-insensitive `FROM` and a nested function. The algorithmic change is trivially O(1) extra work per node and termination is unchanged. Main gaps are literate: the relative-color invariant isn't stated in the code, the `0 + offset` expression reads as a comment-in-arithmetic rather than a named index, and a nested-relative-color test would close the last corner. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT; no behavior change required to merge.
